plant.cvs: 'Mountain Fire' – bright red new growth · 'Katsura' – wine-red young leaves, pink flowers · 'Valley Valentine' – deep pink-red flowers · 'Debutante' – compact, upright flower sprays · 'Little Heath' – dwarf, variegated leaves
plant.foliage: evergreen; glossy narrow leaves, scarlet when young, maturing to dark green
plant.hardinessNote: Hardy in a cold winter throughout most of the UK, approximately -15 to -10°C, though new spring shoots can be scorched by late frost.
plant.prune: Little needed. Lightly trim after flowering to remove spent flower sprays and cut any frost-damaged shoots back to healthy growth.
plant.resilience: Hardy evergreen, but the new growth is scorched by late frost and cold wind. Needs acid soil and yellows on lime. Pests: Pieris lace bug, vine weevil; Phytophthora root rot in wet soil.
plant.soilWarning: Shelter from cold wind and late frost

plant.toxicity: All parts are toxic if eaten, especially the leaves and nectar. They can cause vomiting, drooling and a slowed heart rate in children, dogs, cats, horses and livestock.
